observations.statement: Positive examples alone cannot refute an arbitrary classifier for a nontrivial language because the all-accepting classifier has no false negatives.
Error polarity is not free: an arbitrary wrong SAT circuit may have only false positives, as witnessed by the constant-one circuit.
A positive-only SAT anti-checker can remain logically sufficient for SAT circuit lower bounds only after restricting the quantified circuits to SAT-sound circuits.
The soundness promise does not solve construction: a finite positive list itself induces a sound hardcoded membership circuit whose size must be explicitly charged.
Genesis continuity can preserve research state, but fictional unlimited time is not evidence for a mathematical theorem; every returned claim still requires an explicit proof or counterexample.
